analysis:
The only changed hunk is in SSDPrefixCache.swift evictOldestEntry (head lines 1773-1778). The inline victim-iteration loop is replaced by a call to SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.evictOldest(index:) with a closure that calls retireIndexedEntries([url]). The supplied BASE text covers lines 1838+, and the HEAD text covers only lines 1-656, so the changed head region and the new SSDOwnedEntryRetirement helper were not directly visible. The patch excerpt does show the change. Base behavior: iterate index.oldestEntries(); abort with 0 if retired.externalChange; return on the first entry with indexedBytesFreed > 0 (counting one eviction); skip victims that are valid but undeletable.

Security relevance (T-041, SEC-035): this is the box-wide LRU disk-budget purge of at-rest ciphertext, and TTL/LRU deletion is a stated mitigation. The delegated helper must preserve three properties: it must not delete outside the pinned safe root (retireIndexedEntries/removeItemIfSafe still enforce that), it must still skip undeletable victims so the budget cannot stall, and it must still abort on an external change. I could not verify any of these. Unchanged retirement paths in the supplied base text (scanOnDisk, sweepExpiredEntries, performIndexedRemoval, which uses ownsEvictionRoot) were reviewed and still use the safe-path checks. The head text shown (lifecycle, lookup, endAdoption, close) is unchanged context, and I saw no regression there.

Open question for integration: does SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.evictOldest keep the bounded iteration, skip-on-failure and externalChange semantics, and return indexedBytesFreed? A weakened version would only cause a disk-budget availability or retention regression, with no confidentiality break. No concrete finding is supported by the visible evidence.
